title: Scope 2: separating Ona's core from Supabase

requirements.expectation: The full inventory of direct-access paths (27 backend* functions in app-api.ts) is classified, the 9 in-scope functions are identified, and the requirements below are agreed before implementation starts.
requirements.verification: Stakeholder review of reports/Ona-Scope-2-Stage-1-Review-Guide.html and this guide.
evidence: Approved by stakeholder on 2026-10-10 ("let's begin work") after review of the Stage 1 inventory and this guide. Stage 2 implementation started the same day.

requirements.expectation: No direct browser business writes remain in the 9 in-scope functions, and no error path silently restores a removed fallback (backendFetchPros, backendSetProOnline).
requirements.verification: Diff review of each in-scope function; grep for remaining .from(...) writes; trace every catch/fallback branch.
evidence: Done (9 of 9, all in-scope functions): backendSetProOnline's direct repair_pro_profiles write fallback is removed (app-api.ts) and pro-live-patch.ts/its test deleted as dead code; backendSendMessage's direct messages insert + conversations update are replaced by a call to /api/messages/send; backendFetchPros's direct repair_pro_profiles/profiles read fallback is removed — it now only calls /api/pros and returns [] on any failure, matching the dependency-free behavior /api/pros already provides (tier/suspension/synthetic-account filtering, dual-role self-exclusion); backendGetProOnline's direct repair_pro_profiles read is replaced by a new GET /api/pros/live route that derives the caller from requireUser(req), never a client-supplied id (covered by src/app/api/pros/__tests__/live.test.ts); backendDualRoleFlags's direct motorist_profiles/repair_pro_profiles reads are replaced by a new GET /api/account/role-flags route, same requireUser-derived-caller rule, reusing the exact resolvePrimaryAccountType call the original client code made (covered by src/app/api/account/role-flags/__tests__/route.test.ts); backendFetchJobsForUser's direct service_requests/profiles reads are replaced by a new GET /api/requests route — the same query and mapRequestRow mapping, just run server-side with an explicit userId===session 403 check (mirroring /api/jobs GET's existing convention) instead of relying on browser RLS (covered by src/app/api/requests/__tests__/route.test.ts); backendFetchConversations's direct conversations/messages/profiles/service_requests reads are replaced by a new GET /api/conversations route — the exact same batch queries and mapConversationToThread mapping, run server-side with the same userId===session 403 check (covered by src/app/api/conversations/__tests__/route.test.ts); backendEnsureConversation's direct conversations read+insert is replaced by a new POST /api/conversations/ensure route that derives the caller from requireUser(req) and, unlike the original client function, takes ONLY requestId from the client — motorist_id/repair_pro_id are read from the service_requests row itself rather than trusted from client input, closing a gap the original function had (any caller could previously pass arbitrary motoristId/repairProId values), covered by src/app/api/conversations/ensure/__tests__/route.test.ts including a test that deliberately sends wrong party ids and asserts the insert uses the row's real ones; backendLoadUserProfile's three-table read (profiles/motorist_profiles/repair_pro_profiles/repair_pro_guarantors) is replaced by a new GET /api/profile route that accepts NO client-supplied userId at all, not even as a cross-check, given the sensitivity of the payload (bank account numbers, NIN/BVN, gov-ID URLs, guarantor info) — covered by src/app/api/profile/__tests__/route.test.ts.

Every one of the 9 replacement functions returns its existing safe default (null/[]/{error}) on any route failure, with no fallback to a direct Supabase call — verified per-function during implementation, consistent with the rule that motivated removing backendFetchPros's and backendSetProOnline's fallbacks in the first place.

requirements.expectation: Unauthorized users cannot access or modify another account's jobs, conversations or private profile information once access moves server-side.
requirements.verification: Route-level authorization tests; attempted cross-account access against staging.
evidence: /api/messages/send explicitly checks that the authenticated sender is the conversation's motorist_id or repair_pro_id before inserting, since its service-role client bypasses the RLS check the direct browser write relied on. Covered by a unit test (403 for a non-member sender) in src/app/api/messages/__tests__/send.test.ts.
/api/requests and /api/conversations (GET) both check userId===session 403 before querying, covered by unit tests in their respective __tests__ directories.

/api/conversations/ensure (POST) checks the caller is the service_requests row's motorist_id or repair_pro_id, and derives both party ids for the conversation from that row rather than from client input — covered by a test that sends deliberately wrong client-supplied party ids and asserts the insert uses the row's real ones (src/app/api/conversations/ensure/__tests__/route.test.ts).

/api/profile (GET), which returns the most sensitive data of any in-scope function (bank account numbers, NIN/BVN, gov-ID URLs, guarantor info), accepts no client-supplied userId at all -- the strictest form of the ownership check, since there is no id to mismatch.

All 9 in-scope functions now have a code-level authorization check. What remains for this requirement: staging cross-account attempts have not been run for any of the 9 (the verification method explicitly calls for this), and none of this work has been through independent review yet.

requirements.expectation: Database grants and RLS policies match the intended API and realtime access boundaries; revoking a direct-table grant does not break a realtime subscription that still needs it.
requirements.verification: Diff RLS policies/grants against the finalized access list; confirm each realtime channel (messages, jobs, pro presence) still authenticates after any revocation.

requirements.expectation: Payment atomicity, job version checks, worker ownership and stock reservation behavior are unchanged.
requirements.verification: Re-run existing concurrency tests in src/lib/server/payments and src/lib/server/jobs/deadlines unchanged.

requirements.expectation: backendSendMessage's insert/conversation-update/notify sequence has an explicit, tested answer for partial failure after moving behind a route, not a relocated copy of the same three unguarded calls.
requirements.verification: Failure-injection test on each of the three steps; confirm no message is left with an unupdated conversation or a silently dropped notification.
evidence: /api/messages/send treats the message insert as authoritative (failure returns 500, notify is skipped) and the conversation-timestamp update and notify call as best-effort (failure is logged via serverLogger.warn with outcome context, not silently swallowed, and does not fail an already-delivered message). Covered by src/app/api/messages/__tests__/send.test.ts: insert failure returns 500 and skips notify; conversation-update failure still returns 200 and asserts the warning was logged with the exact event/context.

requirements.expectation: Pros with docs_status 'under_review' or 'rejected' are only shown to customers within DOCS_PENDING_MAX_RADIUS_KM (2 km), not the full marketplace radius.
requirements.verification: Unit test asserting /api/pros excludes a docs-pending pro beyond 2 km but within the normal 5 km radius; code review of the distance filter.
evidence: Fixed in src/app/api/pros/route.ts by dynamically capping maxAllowedRadius to DOCS_PENDING_MAX_RADIUS_KM (2 km) when docsStatus is under_review or rejected. Verified by src/app/api/pros/__tests__/route.test.ts (pro at 1.3 km included, pros at 2.8 km excluded). See docs/review-guides/pros-docs-pending-radius-filter.md.

requirements.expectation: Client and route contracts agree; failed saves are reported accurately. The notification-settings nested/flat field mismatch is fixed, not deferred.
requirements.verification: Contract test for the notification-settings payload shape; assert the client checks the response before showing "saved".

requirements.expectation: Business services in the agreed scope use defined interfaces rather than Supabase SDK types or clients directly.
requirements.verification: Manual import audit of src/lib/server/{jobs,payments,pairing,shop,identity} and the new interface layer.

requirements.expectation: Code checks, browser regression checks, hosted verification and rollout/rollback evidence are recorded separately; unrun checks remain pending.
requirements.verification: This guide's evidence fields are updated per requirement rather than a single blanket status.

implementationNotes: Stage 1 approved 2026-10-10. Stage 2 complete and committed (facb735). Stage 3 complete and committed: backendGetProOnline -> GET /api/pros/live (3f06d8a); backendDualRoleFlags -> GET /api/account/role-flags (3408812); backendFetchJobsForUser -> GET /api/requests (fb72489, a new route rather than reusing /api/jobs's different JobRecord shape); backendFetchConversations -> GET /api/conversations (fc2ec4b); backendEnsureConversation -> POST /api/conversations/ensure (6895db5, closes a party-id trust gap the original function had); backendLoadUserProfile -> GET /api/profile (no client-supplied userId accepted at all, given the sensitivity of the payload). All 9 of 9 in-scope backend* functions no longer call Supabase directly from the browser. Full suite (1,261 tests, 113 files), typecheck and lint all pass locally.
implementationState: Stage 3 complete — 9 of 9 in-scope functions moved; local checks pass; final function (backendLoadUserProfile) uncommitted pending this update
